note: Solomon Islands, read on the Immigration Division's own pages (immigration.gov.sb) on 2026-10-30; its fees are stated in US dollars, so the file's currency is USD. Musicians and bands coming to perform for commercial purposes take the Entertainer Visa (Musician, Commercial): a US$400 visa fee and a US$50 online fee (kept together as US$450, the two parts summed), a permitted stay of 60 days (the term kept), valid up to 2 years with multiple entries, on a sponsor's letter. Its work rights are 'Permitted (entertainment-specific)' and it 'does not permit non-entertainment work': that is neither any work nor work for one sponsor, so the form's work is left out. An extension needs a re-application, so it isn't marked renewable; the page doesn't say from where it is applied for (left out). Long-term employment: the Working Resident Visa for one holding a work permit from the Commissioner of Labour, US$450 plus the US$50 online fee (US$500), valid 2 years, extended in the islands in accordance with the work permit's terms for US$500 (renewable); 'You must apply outside of Solomon Islands' (abroad). Its work rights are 'as defined in Work Permit', and any change in employment must be reported; the page doesn't say the work is tied to one employer, so work is left out (an earlier draft read it in and was held). The Permanent Resident Visa (Resident, Long Term) is for one lawfully resident at least five consecutive years on other visa types, 'e.g., work, study, business' (5 kept as the long-term employment visa's years to it): US$1,500 plus US$50 online (US$1,550), valid 5 years, 'renewable after 5 years'. Its work rights are 'Not automatically granted – assessed based on visa history and compliance', so work is left out; where it is applied for isn't stated (left out). No decision time is published ('there is no specific timeframe'). Naturalisation's years aren't on the pages read.

sources.title: Solomon Islands Immigration Division, Entertainer Visa – Musician (Commercial)
sources.said: This visa is for musicians or bands visiting the Solomon Islands to perform for commercial purposes such as concerts, gigs, or promotional events. ... Visa fee: $400 USD ... Online fee: $50 USD ... Permitted stay: 60 days ... Valid for: Up to 2 years ... re-application required ... Permitted (entertainment-specific) ... Letter from sponsor. ... This visa does not permit non-entertainment work.

sources.title: Solomon Islands Immigration Division, Working Resident Visa – Long-Term Employment
sources.said: The Long-Term Employment Visa allows foreign nationals to reside and work in the Solomon Islands for an extended period under a valid work permit. ... Visa fee: $450 USD ... Online fee: $50 USD ... Visa validity: 2 years ... in accordance with work permit terms ... $500 USD ... Required to submit extension application while you are currently in Solomon Islands. ... Permitted (as defined in Work Permit) ... You must apply outside of Solomon Islands. ... The processing time may vary for different visa categories, there is no specific timeframe ... Any changes in employment must be reported to immigration authorities.

sources.title: Solomon Islands Immigration Division, Permanent Resident Visa – Resident (Long Term)
sources.said: This visa is for individuals who have lawfully resided in the Solomon Islands for at least ... five consecutive years ... on other valid visa types and are now seeking permanent residency. ... Visa fee: $1,500 USD ... Online fee: $50 USD ... Visa validity: 5 years ... Yes – renewable after 5 years ... Not automatically granted – assessed based on visa history and compliance ... on valid visa types (e.g., work, study, business) and wish to transition to long-term residency.
